item.title: Remotely unplugging a USB device on my Mac, without touching it
item.description: Tonight I was remote debugging a USB-C device with custom firmware, which was plugged into my Mac Studio at work. I was accessing it over a WireGuard VPN tunnel. Part of the debugging process involves flashing firmware to the device using MIDI SysEx messages, and while handy, this technique can also be flaky, leaving the device in a partially-flashed state that needs a physical re-plug to recover from.

item.title: Company Culture = Slack Emoji ÷ √Headcount
item.description: Companies spend an enormous amount of time and money trying to measure - and even worse, decide - culture. Engagement surveys, pulse checks, eNPS, offsites where someone from HR asks you to describe the company as a type of animal. Office posters make claims like “our culture is honesty, hard work and fun”, embarrassing the paper they’re printed on. I once applied to a company that asked candidates which kitchen utensil they most identified as, in order to decide if they were a “culture fit”. I never found out what the right answer was, but I got the job after choosing a meat cleaver, so I’m not sure what that says about either of us.

item.title: Optimizing Rustc's next trait solver
item.description:
The next rust trait solver, a large subsystem of the rust compiler that we've been trying to replace, will finally land in rust 1.102.0. In the last stages, before stabilizing it, its performance was a major blocker. But what is "a trait solver"? And why is its performance a problem? My goal for this blog post is to answer those questions in a way where you don't need any prior knowledge. I think discussions of the trait solver can quickly become quite involved, and daunting. So today, we'll start from the very basics!
